examples.label: Verify permissions on a flagged service binary

notes:
=== SharpUp — Automated Privilege Escalation Audit ===
C# port of PowerUp focused exclusively on privilege escalation misconfigurations.

=== WHAT SHARPUP CHECKS ===
.\SharpUp.exe audit runs all checks:
- ModifiableServices → service objects with write access for current user
- ModifiableServiceBinaries → service binaries with write access
- UnquotedServicePath → services with unquoted paths containing spaces
- ModifiableRegistryAutoRuns → autorun registry keys with write access
- ModifiableAutoRuns → autorun binary paths with write access
- AlwaysInstallElevated → both HKCU and HKLM keys set to 1
- TokenPrivileges → non-standard privileges in current token
- ProcessDLLHijack → processes loading DLLs from writable locations
- RegistryAutoLogon → Autologon credentials stored in registry

Individual check:
  .\SharpUp.exe audit ModifiableServiceBinaries

=== COMPARISON WITH POWERUP ===
PowerUp.ps1 → Invoke-AllChecks  (PowerShell — use when C# execution is blocked)
SharpUp     → .\SharpUp.exe audit  (C# — harder for script-based controls to block)
winPEAS     → broader coverage, noisier, includes non-privesc findings

=== OPERATIONAL NOTES ===
AV often flags SharpUp by signature — compile fresh from source or use obfuscation
Run immediately after landing foothold — don't wait for manual enumeration
Save output: .\SharpUp.exe audit | Tee-Object sharpup-out.txt
Cross-reference findings with icacls and accesschk to confirm before exploiting

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
SharpUp identifies → manual verify with icacls/accesschk → select exploit path
ModifiableServiceBinaries → weak binary replacement → SYSTEM
UnquotedServicePath + writable directory → place binary at candidate path → SYSTEM
AlwaysInstallElevated → msfvenom MSI → SYSTEM
TokenPrivileges → SeImpersonate → Potato attack → SYSTEM

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
Any finding from SharpUp = immediate exploitation attempt
Multiple findings on same host = escalation path redundancy (exploit the easiest one first)
No SharpUp findings → move to: kernel exploits, credential hunting, DLL hijacking
SharpUp on service accounts → different token → may reveal different writable paths

recommended.note: Exploit a weak service ACL (reconfigure binPath).

name: Weak Permissions - SharpUp Audit
description: SharpUp flags modifiable service binaries, weak service/registry ACLs, unquoted paths, and AlwaysInstallElevated. Confirm any hit with icacls before exploiting.

defense.why_it_works: SharpUp is a C# port of PowerUp that performs automated Windows privilege escalation checks. It identifies misconfigured services, unquoted service paths, AlwaysInstallElevated, writable service binaries, registry ACL weaknesses, and token privilege abuse opportunities in a single scan. Typically run as the first post-exploitation enumeration step.
defense.prerequisites: Shell access. SharpUp.exe binary available. Standard user or admin — checks different findings at each level.
defense.impact: Comprehensive enumeration of privilege escalation vectors — identifies which subsequent attacks are applicable, significantly speeding up the escalation process.
defense.detection: SharpUp.exe execution (known tool signature, 25+ AV detections). Large number of service and registry queries in rapid succession. EDR: privilege escalation enumeration pattern.
defense.artifacts: Process: SharpUp.exe executed by standard user | Series of WMI/registry queries against service configurations | EDR: tool signature match for SharpUp
defense.prevention: Deploy AV/EDR that detects SharpUp execution. Fix underlying misconfigurations that SharpUp identifies. Run SharpUp defensively on a regular schedule to proactively detect misconfigurations before attackers do.
defense.misconfiguration: No EDR detecting known privilege escalation enumeration tools. Underlying misconfigurations (weak service permissions, unquoted paths, AlwaysInstallElevated) present that SharpUp would identify.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# SharpUp audit:
.\SharpUp.exe audit
# Output:
# [!] Modifiable Service Binaries: C:\Tools\svc.exe (Everyone: GenericWrite)
# [!] Unquoted Service Paths: 'C:\Program Files\Vuln App\service.exe'
# [!] AlwaysInstallElevated: 1 in HKCU and HKLM
defense.secure_config:
# Run SharpUp defensively to find misconfigurations:
.\SharpUp.exe audit > C:\Reports\privesc_findings.txt

# Then remediate findings:
# Weak service binary: icacls <path> to restrict permissions
# Unquoted paths: update service config to quote the binary path
# AlwaysInstallElevated: disable in both registry keys
defense.evasion: Restore the original service binary/ACL/registry value after execution; trigger via a scheduled restart instead of an obvious sc stop/start; name the payload to blend with the legitimate service.

steps.label: Follow the highest-signal finding
